newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey stresses need for low U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey stresses need for low U.S. inflation.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey on Friday stressed the importance of low inflation for the long-term health of the U.S. economy.
"I don't think there is any substitute in the world today for a low inflation environment," Lindsey told the Atlantic Economic Conference.
Low inflation helps long-term planning and promotes more efficient use of capital, Lindsey said.
He said the Fed faces competition from other central banks in its pursuit of low inflation.
If the U.S. falls behind Germany and Japan in the battle against inflation, it risks the dollar losing its status as the world's key reserve currency, he said.
Echoing a theme he struck earlier in the day, Lindsey called for a more productive U.S. government.
Rather than focusing on cutting the budget deficit, the U.S. government needs to focus on how it is spending its money, he said.
